hook_text: 2 to the power negative 3. Is it minus 8? Minus an eighth? Keep halving and the answer is obvious.
clip_script: Start with 2 cubed, 8. Drop the exponent by one, halve the answer: 4. Again: 2. Again: 1 — that is 2 to the power zero. Now refuse to stop. Exponent negative 1: a half. Negative 2: a quarter. Negative 3: an eighth. Nothing crashed, nothing went negative. The numbers just got small. So 2 to the power negative 3 is one eighth — one over 2 cubed. A negative exponent means hop to the other side of the fraction bar and make the exponent positive. Only the factor carrying the minus hops: 3 times x to the power negative 2 is 3 over x squared, the 3 stays on top. And a negative exponent makes a number small, never negative. Tattoo that one.
visual_style: A column of powers of 2 counts down on a whiteboard, each value halving, crossing a glowing zero line into fractions; then a fraction bar drawn as a fence with a power hopping over it and its minus sign flipping to plus.
pacing: Steady halving beat, then one crisp hop, then the tattoo line held.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and never write a minus sign where a fraction belongs.
